INDICATION
Mr. Castellanos-Reyes is a 47-year-old night-shift dispatcher at Tri-County Ready-Mix who fell asleep at the wheel driving home after a shift; his car struck a utility pole on Sept. 3rd, 2026 (chest-wall contusion, treated and released from the ED). His wife Marisol reports loud snoring and witnessed apneas for >5 years. Epworth 17/24. PMH: Hodgkin lymphoma (ABVD, 2011), in remission; HTN; GERD. BMI 41.3 kg/m2, neck 18.5 in, Mallampati IV, BP 148/92.

TECHNIQUE
Attended in-lab study: EEG (F4-M1, C4-M1, O2-M1), EOG, chin and tibialis EMG, ECG, oronasal thermistor, nasal pressure, RIP belts, oximetry, position and synchronized video. Scored per AASM Manual v3, hypopneas with 3% desaturation or arousal (rule 1A). Split criteria met at 01:12 after 148.5 min.

DIAGNOSTIC PORTION (TST 131.0 min)
Sleep efficiency 88.5%, sleep latency 6.5 min, REM 9%.
AHI 52.7/h (supine 71.4/h, non-supine 24.0/h); RDI 58.1/h.
Obstructive apneas 61, central 3, mixed 2, hypopneas 49.
ODI (3%) 48.9/h. SpO2 baseline 94%, nadir 76%, T88 19.6 min.
HR 58-104 bpm, occasional PVCs. No Cheyne-Stokes respiration. PLM index 4/h.

CPAP TITRATION (TST 187.5 min)
Started CPAP 5 cm H2O, medium nasal mask, raised in 1 cm steps; switched to full-face mask at 02:40 for mouth leak.
  9 cm H2O  - 22.0 min - AHI 18.5 - nadir 87%
 11 cm H2O  - 31.5 min - AHI 6.7  - nadir 90%
 12 cm H2O  - 48.0 min - AHI 1.3  - nadir 93% (supine REM seen)
 13 cm H2O  - 34.0 min - AHI 0.0  - nadir 94%

IMPRESSION
1. Severe obstructive sleep apnea, AHI 52.7/h, ODI 48.9/h, supine-predominant, with marked hypoxemia.
2. Effective CPAP 12 cm H2O (residual AHI 1.3/h, ODI 1.9/h).
3. Excessive sleepiness with a recent drowsy-driving collision.

RECOMMENDATIONS
- CPAP 12 cm H2O, heated humidity, medium full-face mask; acceptable alternative APAP 10-15 cm H2O.
- No driving while drowsy until adherent and Epworth <10; discussed with patient and Marisol.
- Weight management referral. Sleep clinic follow-up in 6-8 weeks with download.

Dear Dr Hope,

RE: PĀTENE, Wiremu Hōri ("Bill") · NHI ZRT4471 · DOB 07.05.1935 (91 yrs)
12B Huia Terrace, Cashmere, Christchurch 8022 · mob 021 448 3196
Study no. SASC-26-0918 · attended video-polysomnography, night of 8–9 September 2026

Thank you for referring this 91-year-old retired orchardist who lives with his wife Hinemoa in a villa at Rata Grove Retirement Village, Halswell. For about two years she has seen him shout, punch and kick in his sleep, apparently acting out dreams. On 22 August he fell out of bed during one of these episodes and struck his head on the bedside cabinet (small occipital laceration closed with Steri-Strips by the village nurse, no loss of consciousness). She also describes loud snoring. Home oximetry at Avonhead Respiratory Clinic in March 2019 was unremarkable. Epworth 7/24, MoCA 26/30, BP 136/74. No tremor, bradykinesia or hyposmia on your examination.

The study (lights out 21:58, lights on 06:04) was set up by Kiri Parkinson, RPSGT. Total sleep time was 5 h 41 min with sleep efficiency 72% and frequent spontaneous arousals. REM made up 14% of sleep.

Breathing: AHI 21.6/h (supine 34.2/h, lateral 9.8/h, REM 28.0/h), mostly obstructive hypopnoeas; central AHI 1.1/h. ODI (3%) 18.4/h, mean SpO2 93%, nadir 82%, T90 3.1%. No periodic breathing.

REM: tonic and phasic chin EMG activity in 46% of REM epochs, i.e. REM sleep without atonia. At 03:27 the video shows shouting and arm flailing in REM, not preceded by a respiratory event. PLMS index 11/h. Sinus rhythm 54–78/min with occasional APBs.

Impression
1. REM sleep behaviour disorder, confirmed on video-PSG.
2. Moderate obstructive sleep apnoea, supine and REM predominant.
3. Fall from bed on 22 August due to dream enactment.

Plan
- Bed safety: lower the bed, mattress or padding beside it, move the cabinet away; Hinemoa may prefer a separate bed for now.
- Melatonin 3 mg at bedtime, up to 6 mg. I would avoid clonazepam at his age given falls risk.
- Four-week APAP loan via our CPAP clinic, min 6 / max 13 cmH2O, EPR 2, nasal pillows; we will review the download. If tolerated, fixed CPAP 10 cmH2O is a reasonable longer-term setting.
- RBD can precede Parkinson disease or dementia with Lewy bodies. I raised this gently with Bill and Hinemoa and suggest yearly review for motor or cognitive change.

I hope this is helpful. I am happy to discuss on 03 365 0848 or physicians@southernalpssleep.co.nz.

Ngā mihi nui,

Dr Anaïs Duval, FRACP
Sleep and Respiratory Physician
